cover.headline: A well-run fertiliser leader in a subsidy squeeze, priced as if the squeeze were over
cover.lead: Coromandel is India's largest private phosphatic fertiliser maker (Nutrient & allied, ~87% of revenue and ~84% of segment EBITDA in FY26) with a fast-growing crop protection arm that now includes 53%-owned NACL Industries. Q1FY27 showed both sides: crop protection had a record quarter (standalone EBIT +44%), but fertiliser profit fell 24% as Middle East-driven ammonia, sulphur and phosphoric acid costs ran ahead of a 10% subsidy increase. The 2026 monsoon ended at 87% of normal (76% in the south, Coromandel's core market), and rabi subsidy rates were still unannounced on 30-Sep. We value Coromandel the way the street does, on **P/E: 15x Sep-28E EPS of ₹87.5**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹1,609) and DCF (₹1,711) are higher but also below the share price. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Fertiliser margins are set in Delhi, not Chennai
arguments.p: About 77% of Q1FY27 revenue was subsidised fertiliser. The government fixes the subsidy per kg of nutrient (NBS) and, in practice, the farm-gate price. Kharif 2026 rates rose ~10% while phosphoric acid rose from $1,360 to $1,700 a tonne; Nutrient PBIT fell 24% to ₹479 cr (6.9% margin vs 9.9%). Rabi rates were unknown on 30-Sep. Manufactured EBITDA was "₹5,000 plus" per tonne in FY26 and below ₹3,500 in Q4.

arguments.h: Backward integration helps, but adds costs first
arguments.p: The new Kakinada sulphuric and phosphoric acid plants (60% of acid needs), the Senegal rock mine and a 7.5 lakh t granulation train (Q4FY27) should lift EBITDA per tonne towards management's ₹6,500 target. But D&A jumped to ₹203 cr in Q1FY27 (₹121 cr a year earlier) from the acid plants, mine amortisation and NACL intangibles, so EPS lags EBITDA. We model fertiliser EBITDA margins of 9.2% / 11.0% / 11.2% (FY27-29E): back to FY25 levels, not above.

arguments.h: Crop protection is the growth engine, but still small
arguments.p: Crop protection revenue rose 50% to ₹3,968 cr in FY26 (NACL from Aug-2025) and standalone EBIT margin is ~19%. We model +30% / +14% / +12% at a 15.5-16.5% EBITDA margin; NACL earns ~11% and 46% of it belongs to minorities. Even by FY29E, crop protection is only ~22% of segment EBITDA: not enough to make Coromandel an "agrochemical" stock.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street pays for a recovery we cannot yet see
arguments.p: Brokers use 25-30x FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal 25x on ~₹101.2 implied). Our FY28E EPS of ₹81.1 is 20% lower because we charge the higher D&A and finance cost and assume only partial subsidy relief. The stock's one-year-forward P/E median since 2021 is 17.5x; fertiliser and agrochemical peers trade ~14% below their own medians. At ₹1,758 it trades at 21.7x our FY28E.

catalysts: Rabi 2026-27 NBS subsidy rates (due before the October-March season): the single biggest swing factor for H2FY27 fertiliser margins.
Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Kharif-season margins at a $1,700/t phosphoric acid price; subsidy receivables.
Rabi demand in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka after a monsoon at 76% of normal in the south peninsula and low reservoirs.
Commissioning of the 7.5 lakh t granulation train (Q4FY27) and stable running of the new phosphoric acid plant.
Clarity on the government's "reasonable margin" guidelines for P&K fertilisers (a possible profit cap).

sections.title: A phosphatic fertiliser franchise with a crop protection business attached

blocks.p: Coromandel makes and sells phosphatic fertilisers (DAP and NPK "complex" grades) from two large complexes at Visakhapatnam and Kakinada, sells single super phosphate (SSP) from eight smaller plants, and trades imported DAP, urea and potash. Around this core it sells specialty and organic nutrients, nano DAP, drone spraying and ~1,200 own retail stores, mostly in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The crop protection segment makes technicals (mancozeb is the largest) and branded formulations, sells B2B and exports, and since August 2025 consolidates NACL Industries. It is a Murugappa group company: E.I.D. Parry owns 55.6%.

blocks.p: **Fertilisers are a regulated conversion business.** Coromandel buys phosphoric acid, ammonia, sulphur and rock phosphate (largely imported), converts them into DAP and NPK, and sells at a maximum retail price that is effectively capped. The government pays a subsidy per kg of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potash (K) and sulphur (S) under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme, revised every season. Profit per tonne = MRP + subsidy − raw-material cost − conversion cost. When global raw materials jump and the subsidy lags (FY23, Q4FY26-Q1FY27), margins compress; when policy catches up, they recover. **Crop protection is a chemistry and brands business**: technicals compete on cost with China, branded formulations on distribution and new products. It is not subsidised and can pass on costs, which is why its margins are steadier.

sections.title: Indian fertilisers: steady demand, imported inputs, and a subsidy that sets the margin

blocks.p: India used 71 mt of fertilisers in FY26 (POS sales), up from 63 mt in FY23. Urea (40 mt) is fully price-controlled; DAP (9 mt), NPK complexes (14 mt) and SSP (5.5 mt) are under the NBS scheme. NPKs have taken share from DAP and are now ~60% of phosphatics. Two features matter for Coromandel. **First, inputs are imported:** India relies on imports for more than 80% of its ammonia and sulphur and much of its phosphoric acid and rock, so costs follow world prices and the rupee (₹92.6-96.8 per $ in Q1FY27). **Second, the margin is a policy outcome:** the government revises NBS rates each season, and in a cost spike it decides how much of the increase the industry absorbs. In Q1FY27 industry DAP+NPK production fell 21% and imports 38% because the Kharif 2026 rates (+~10%) did not cover the Middle East-driven jump in costs.

bullets: **Volume leader.** Record DAP+NPK sales of 4.3 mt in FY26 (+7%), 17.5% of consumption, and record production of 3.5 mt. In Q1FY27 it deliberately cut production to 6.9 lakh t (72% utilisation) to avoid high-cost inventory; volumes fell 9% but primary share rose to 22% (18%).

**Margins are the problem.** Segment EBITDA margin: 10.1% (FY23), 11.8% (FY24), 11.5% (FY25), 10.8% (FY26). Manufactured EBITDA was "₹5,000 plus" a tonne in FY26 and below ₹3,500 in Q4FY26; trading earns 4-5%. Management's ₹6,500 target needs normal raw-material prices.

**Subsidy dependence.** Government subsidy was ₹11,139 cr of the segment's ₹27,727 cr revenue in FY26 (40%); the subsidy business was 85% of FY26 revenue and 66% of EBITDA (77% and 48% in Q1FY27). Receivables from the government: ₹2,168 cr (Mar-26), ₹3,254 cr (Jun-26).

**Beyond DAP/NPK.** SSP 8.4 lakh t (#1, >50% premium grades, ₹2,500-3,000/t); specialty nutrients +25-30% a year at ~20% margin; nano DAP ~50-60% share but banned in UP and Maharashtra; ~1,200 retail stores (revenue +85% in Q1FY27); Senegal rock now consolidated.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** a strong franchise with no pricing power. We model revenue +10% / +8% / +7% (FY27-29E) and EBITDA margin 9.2% / 11% / 11.2%: FY27 absorbs the subsidy gap in H1 and a weak southern rabi; FY28-29 benefit from own acid, Senegal rock and the granulation train, but stay at FY25 margin levels. Every 1 point of Nutrient margin moves FY28E EPS by ~₹8.3.

sections.title: Backward integration: the right strategy, with the costs arriving first

blocks.p: Coromandel spent ~₹7,000 cr in three to four years (management) on four things: (1) a 2,000 TPD sulphuric acid and 650 TPD (~2 lakh t a year) phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada, commissioned in March 2026, which lifts own acid to ~60% of needs; (2) control of BMCC, a rock phosphate mine in Senegal (71.5%), producing 3.5 lakh t in FY26 and heading for ~5 lakh t; (3) a 7.5 lakh t granulation train at Kakinada, due in Q4FY27, half to be sold through its own stores; (4) NACL Industries (₹820 cr). Smaller projects: a technical MAP plant, seaweed granulation, mancozeb capacity and a fluorination launch plant for CDMO.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the logic is sound: owning acid and rock removes the most volatile part of the cost base, and the ~2-year payback discussed on the Q2FY26 call ($250-300 of margin per tonne of acid on ~₹1,000-1,100 cr of capex, i.e. up to ~₹500 cr a year on ~2 lakh t) is plausible at normal sulphur prices. But in Q1FY27 sulphur was so expensive that the new acid plant ran at moderate rates, and the new assets added ~₹80 cr a quarter of depreciation and amortisation. We give the projects credit from FY28 (Nutrient margin 11.0%) rather than in FY27.

bullets: **Standalone is strong.** Revenue ₹3,054 cr in FY26 (+16%), PBIT ₹569 cr (+55%, 19% margin); Q1FY27 revenue +20% to ₹870 cr and EBIT +44% to ₹159 cr on exports, B2B and price pass-through. New products were 32% of domestic B2C sales. Guidance: 20-25% growth at ~19% margin; 20,000 t more mancozeb at Sarigam.

**NACL is a turnaround, not yet a compounder.** Bought for ₹820 cr (53%) at ₹76.70 a share; a ₹250 cr rights issue cut its debt. FY26 revenue ₹1,585 cr, EBITDA ₹103 cr; Q1FY27 revenue ₹383 cr (export prices weaker), EBITDA ₹41 cr (11%). Management: 11% is a "reasonable level"; more needs new products over 2-3 years. In consolidation it lost ₹64 cr in FY26 after ~₹80 cr a year of acquisition amortisation, and 46% of its profit belongs to minorities.
**Next steps:** CDMO/fluorination launch plant at Ankleshwar, intermediates for MNCs using NACL's spare capacity, Latin America push. None is quantified.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is the part of Coromandel the bulls are paying for, and it deserves a higher multiple than fertilisers. But it is ~16% of segment EBITDA today and ~22% in FY29E. We model revenue +30% / +14% / +12% and EBITDA margin 15.5% / 16% / 16.5%, taking segment EBITDA from ₹587 cr (FY26) to ₹{{F.seg.cp.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr (FY29E).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Coromandel has a **real but narrow advantage**: the best distribution and brand in South Indian phosphatics, the largest NPK and SSP volumes, a net-cash balance sheet that can carry ₹3,000+ cr of subsidy receivables, and now partial ownership of its raw materials. That makes it the most resilient producer in a downturn (it kept producing in Q1FY27 while the industry cut output by a fifth). It does **not** give pricing power: the government sets the subsidy and, in effect, the price, and reasonable-margin rules cap the upside. In crop protection it is a solid generic player, not an innovator. Expect high-teens ROE through the cycle, not a compounding franchise that re-rates for ever.

sections.title: Revenue has tripled in ten years; profit per rupee of sales has not

blocks.p: Coromandel's revenue rose from ₹11,306 cr in FY15 to ₹31,480 cr in FY26. Most of that is price, not volume: fertiliser prices and subsidies follow global raw materials, so revenue jumped 55% in FY23 (after the Russia-Ukraine war), fell 26% in FY24 and rose 31% in FY26 as the Middle East crisis lifted input prices again. Profit has grown more slowly. Net profit was ₹1,329 cr in FY21 and ₹1,898 cr in FY26 (₹1,956 cr attributable to shareholders), and FY25's ₹2,055 cr included a ₹398 cr land gain. EBITDA margin fell from 14% in FY21 to 10.3% in FY26. Q1FY27 continued the squeeze: revenue +16%, net profit −24% to ₹382 cr.

pair.title: Revenue swings with global fertiliser prices
Net profit: up 43% in five years, flat since FY23
EBITDA margin: 14% in FY21, 10% in FY26
Quarterly profit: Q2 is the big quarter, Q4 the weak one

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a policy-regulated volume business. The government sets the subsidy per kg of nutrient and, in practice, the farm-gate price, so fertiliser margins are squeezed whenever raw materials rise faster than the subsidy (FY23, Q4FY26-Q1FY27) and recover when policy catches up. Growth in profit comes from volume, cost (backward integration) and the non-subsidy businesses (crop protection, specialty nutrients, retail), not from pricing power.

sections.title: The cash pile has gone into acid plants, a mine and an agrochemical company; returns are falling

blocks.p: In FY19-22 Coromandel generated ₹8,616 cr of operating cash and spent only ₹1,002 cr on plants: it repaid ~₹2,560 cr of debt and built a cash pile. In FY23-26 capex rose to ₹3,523 cr (the Kakinada sulphuric and phosphoric acid plants, granulation, crop protection capacity), and it bought control of the Senegal rock mine (BMCC) and 53% of NACL Industries (₹820 cr). Management puts the total at "close to ₹7,000 crores" over three to four years. So far returns have fallen: ROCE was 35-38% in FY22-23 and 22% in FY26, because the new assets are not yet earning and FY26 fertiliser margins were squeezed.

blocks.callout: **The test is FY27-29.** Management says it will now pause big projects ("normal sustainable capex of ₹300 crores") and harvest: own acid for 60% of needs, ~5 lakh t a year of Senegal rock, a 7.5 lakh t granulation train from Q4FY27, and NACL. If fertiliser EBITDA per tonne rises from ~₹5,000 to the targeted ₹6,500, returns recover; if subsidies keep lagging costs, the new assets mainly add depreciation (Q1FY27 D&A ₹203 cr vs ₹121 cr a year earlier).

sections.title: Earnings quality: a clean audit, but one-offs, subsidies and minorities to strip out

bullets: **Subsidy income is 35% of revenue.** ₹11,139 cr of FY26 revenue is government subsidy, recognised on notified NBS rates and DBT sales; the auditor (S.R. Batliboi, EY network) makes its recognition and recoverability a key audit matter. Cash lags: ₹2,168 cr owed at Mar-26 and ₹3,254 cr at Jun-26.

**One-offs in both directions.** FY25 profit includes a ₹397.71 cr gain on assigning leasehold land rights (exceptional) and a ₹50.94 cr asset impairment; FY26 includes a ₹70.56 cr goodwill impairment on the drone subsidiary Dhaksha, booked inside segment profit. Underlying FY25 EPS was therefore lower than reported, and FY26 higher.

**Minorities now matter.** NACL (46% minority) and BMCC (28.5%) are consolidated. In FY26 minorities absorbed ₹58 cr of losses, so profit attributable to shareholders (₹1,956 cr) exceeded total profit (₹1,898 cr). As NACL improves this reverses: minorities will take a share of profit.

**Acquisition and mine amortisation below EBITDA.** ~₹21 cr a quarter of NACL intangibles and ~₹30 cr of Senegal mine overburden run through D&A (Q1FY27). EBITDA growth therefore overstates growth in earnings: Q1FY27 EBITDA −3%, PAT −24%.

**Working capital is funded by suppliers' banks.** ₹5,022 cr of the ₹8,827 cr of trade payables are acceptances (bank-backed credit for imported raw materials); their cost sits in finance cost, which rose from ₹262 cr (FY25) to ₹343 cr (FY26).

**Reasonable-margin guidelines.** The company says it awaits clarity on new government guidelines limiting profit on subsidised P&K fertilisers (note 31.6). A binding cap would make part of today's profit, and of the integration upside, temporary.

**Definitions.** Company EBITDA (₹3,232 cr in FY26) excludes exceptional items and JV share and equals Screener's; the annual report's other income (₹348 cr) includes ~₹16 cr Screener counts as operating.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The books are clean (Big-4-network auditor, contingent liabilities only ₹189 cr) and cash conversion over time is reasonable. But a third of revenue is a government payment at policy-set rates, recent years carry one-offs either way, minorities and acquisition amortisation now separate EBITDA from EPS, and a pending profit cap hangs over the fertiliser margin.

sections.title: Net cash, but the government is the biggest debtor

blocks.p: Coromandel has net cash: at Mar-2026 cash, investments and ₹1,564 cr of inter-corporate deposits with Bajaj Finance exceeded borrowings and leases (₹1,506 cr) by ~₹2,600 cr, down from ~₹4,570 cr a year earlier after the NACL purchase, capex and a build-up of working capital. Working capital is driven by two things it does not control: raw-material prices (inventory rose 51% to ₹7,204 cr in FY26; much of it is funded by ₹5,022 cr of acceptances, i.e. bank-backed supplier credit) and the pace of subsidy payments (₹2,168 cr owed by the government at Mar-2026, ₹3,254 cr at Jun-2026). Borrowings rose to ₹1,506 cr (incl. ₹639 cr of leases) as NACL's debt was consolidated.

sections.title: The street: uniformly positive, on earnings set before the cost shock

blocks.p: Latest call per broker found by 30-Sep-2026: 2 Buys after Q1FY27 (Motilal Oswal ₹2,530, DAM Capital ₹2,750); older Buys from Sharekhan (₹2,900), Nuvama (₹3,234) and Accumulate from Geojit (₹2,548), all set before the Middle East cost shock. No Sell found. Bulls argue that crop protection, backward integration and NACL make Coromandel an "agri-solutions" company worth 25-30x earnings, and that subsidy lags are temporary. We agree the lags are temporary in principle (policy envisages compensating input costs over time), but the fertiliser margin has been on a downward trend since FY21, and the street's FY28 earnings still look closer to the pre-crisis numbers than to the Q1FY27 run-rate.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good company in a squeeze, priced for the recovery

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest private phosphatic fertiliser maker, with the best distribution in the south, a net-cash balance sheet and newly integrated acid and rock supply; plus a crop protection business growing 20%+ (with a half-owned, low-margin NACL attached). Its profits depend on subsidy rates set by the government each season, on imported raw materials and on the monsoon.

**What you are paying:** 21.7x our FY28E EPS and 20.1x Sep-28E, against a one-year-forward median of 17.5x since 2021 and fertiliser peers on ~14.6x trailing. On the street's own method with our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The stock already fell ~10% in the last three trading days of September, but it still prices a fast return to pre-crisis margins.

**Turn neutral (HOLD) below ~₹1,380**, and positive below ~₹1,140, or on evidence that the rabi subsidy and own acid restore fertiliser EBITDA to ₹5,500-6,500/t.
**Biggest swing factor:** the subsidy-adjusted fertiliser margin. Every 1 point of Nutrient & allied EBITDA margin moves FY28E EPS by ~₹8.3 (≈10%).

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Di-ammonium phosphate (18% N, 46% P₂O₅): the most used phosphatic fertiliser; its farm price is held at ₹1,350 a 50 kg bag.
Granular fertilisers that combine nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potash (K) in set grades, e.g. 20:20:0:13.
Single super phosphate: a low-cost phosphatic fertiliser (16% P₂O₅) made from rock phosphate and sulphuric acid.
Urea is the main nitrogen fertiliser (price fully controlled); MOP is muriate of potash. Coromandel trades both.
Nutrient Based Subsidy: the government pays a fixed subsidy per kg of N, P, K and S in each P&K fertiliser, revised every season (kharif: Apr-Sep; rabi: Oct-Mar).
Maximum retail price; for DAP effectively fixed by the government, for NPKs in practice constrained.
Phosphoric acid (from rock phosphate and sulphuric acid) is the main input for DAP/NPK; sulphuric acid is made by burning sulphur.
The nitrogen input for DAP and NPKs; India imports most of it.
Making one's own raw materials (here acid and rock) instead of buying them.
Government rules capping the profit companies may earn on subsidised P&K fertilisers.
In crop protection: the active ingredient (technical) and the ready-to-use product sold to farmers (formulation).
Contract development and manufacturing for other companies.
Inter-corporate deposits: here, deposits placed with Bajaj Finance, counted as cash.
Bank-backed credit from suppliers (usually for imported raw materials), shown within trade payables.
The share of a subsidiary's profit that belongs to its other shareholders (46% of NACL, 28.5% of BMCC).
Profit of a segment before interest, tax and central costs (PBIT); EBITDA adds back the segment's depreciation.
Share price ÷ earnings per share; enterprise value (market value − net cash) ÷ EBITDA.
Discounted cash flow valuation; Ke is the cost of equity (here 11.9% = 6.5% risk-free + 0.9 × 6% equity risk premium).
Long-period average rainfall used by IMD to define a normal monsoon.
exhibit.source: GAM Research

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Coromandel International (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: Nutrient & allied and Crop protection each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment PBIT + segment D&A, excluding impairments). A third line removes inter-segment sales. Group EBITDA = sum of segments less central costs (Screener basis, excluding other income). Valued on P/E, as the street does. Engine workaround: the tax line also carries minorities and a share-count true-up (see _taxWhy).

segments.name: Nutrient & allied
segments._why: FY27: Q1 revenue +9% (prices up 25-30% across grades, DAP+NPK volumes -9% as production was cut to 72% utilisation); rabi demand at risk after a monsoon at 87% of normal (south peninsula 76%) and low southern reservoirs, and imported DAP limited: +10%. FY28 +8%: the 7.5 lakh t granulation train (commissioning Q4FY27) adds volume while prices ease if Middle East supply normalises. FY29 +7%: volume growth from the expanded Kakinada complex and SSP/specialty nutrients.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 14.1% (FY20), 14.8% (FY21), 11.4% (FY22), 10.1% (FY23), 11.8% (FY24), 11.5% (FY25), 10.8% (FY26). Q1FY27 PBIT margin 6.9% vs 9.9% a year earlier as ammonia, sulphur and phosphoric acid ($1,700/t for Q2 vs $1,360) outran a 10% NBS increase. FY27 9.2% assumes only partial relief in H2. FY28 11.0% and FY29 11.2%: own sulphuric/phosphoric acid (60% of needs), Senegal rock and granulation volumes lift EBITDA/t towards ~₹5,500-6,000 (management target ₹6,500), but subsidy policy and reasonable-margin guidelines cap the upside: still below FY24-25 margins on today's higher price base.

segments.name: Crop protection
segments._why: FY27 +30%: a full year of NACL (consolidated from 8-Aug-2025; FY26 NACL revenue ₹1,585 cr, of which ₹923 cr consolidated) plus standalone growth of ~18% (Q1 +20%; guidance 20-25%; 20,000 t mancozeb expansion at Sarigam). FY28 +14% (standalone ~17%, NACL ~5%); FY29 +12%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 15.3-18.7% (FY20-21), 14.0-16.5% (FY22-25), 14.8% in FY26 with NACL's low-margin months and acquisition amortisation-free EBITDA. Standalone PBIT margin ~19% (FY26) and 18% in Q1FY27; NACL EBITDA margin 11% in Q1FY27 ('reasonable level' without new products). Mix-weighted 15.5% / 16.0% / 16.5% as NACL slowly improves.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between the segments removed on consolidation: ₹174 cr (FY24), ₹204 cr (FY25), ₹216 cr (FY26); we assume +10% a year.
segments._marginWhy: Inter-segment profit adjustment has been within ±₹6 cr a year: modelled at zero.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Central costs not allocated to segments (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: ₹310 cr (FY24), ₹335 cr (FY25), ₹343 cr (FY26); reported unallocable expense ₹291 cr / ₹283 cr / ₹359 cr. We assume ₹360-400 cr as corporate, R&D and retail-network costs grow.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 cash capex ₹1,540 cr (Kakinada acid plants). FY27 ₹900 cr = capital commitments of ₹619 cr at Mar-2026 (granulation, T-MAP, mancozeb, fluorination launch plant) plus ~₹300 cr of maintenance; FY28-29 ₹600 cr = management's 'normal sustainable capex of ₹300 crores' for Coromandel plus NACL, Senegal and retail-store spending.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹534 cr = 6.8% of average gross block, but Q1FY27 D&A was ₹203 cr (₹812 cr annualised) as the acid plants (+₹16-18 cr a quarter), NACL acquisition intangibles (~₹21 cr) and Senegal mine overburden (~₹30 cr) came in. 7.8% gives ~₹760 cr / ~₹820 cr / ~₹870 cr for FY27-29.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net treasury at Mar-2026: cash ₹494 cr + investments ₹2,044 cr + ICDs with Bajaj Finance ₹1,564 cr (6.8-8.2%) less borrowings incl. leases ₹1,506 cr = ₹2,596 cr. 6.5% on the opening balance, below the deposit rate because seasonal working capital (subsidy receivables peak in Q2) absorbs part of the cash during the year.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Other income ₹240 cr in FY26 (Screener, normal) and ₹50 cr in Q1FY27 as the cash pile fell after the NACL purchase and capex; ~₹30 cr a year of non-treasury items on top of the treasury yield (FY27E total ~₹200 cr).

otherTreasury.label: Inter-corporate deposits with Bajaj Finance (in other assets)
otherTreasury._why: ICDs of ₹1,564 cr placed with Bajaj Finance at 6.8-8.2% sit in 'loans' (other assets) on Screener; the company itself counts them as cash in its net-debt calculation (note 32.1).

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹343 cr; Q1FY27 ₹89 cr (₹68 cr a year earlier). Most of it is the cost of acceptances and working-capital lines that fund imported raw materials, which cost more at today's prices: ₹400 cr in FY27, easing to ₹370 cr as prices normalise.
assumptions._taxWhy: Underlying tax rate 26% (FY26 27.5% incl. the non-deductible drone impairment; Q1FY27 26%; statutory 25.17% plus subsidiaries' losses without tax credit). Engine workaround: the model has no minority-interest line and takes its share count from FY26 total profit ÷ EPS (₹1,898 cr ÷ ₹66.31 = 28.62 cr shares vs 29.50 cr actual diluted shares, because FY26 profit attributable to owners, ₹1,956 cr, exceeded total profit as minorities absorbed ₹58 cr of losses). So the 'tax' line here = 1 − (28.62 ÷ 29.50) × (1 − 26%) + minorities' share of profit (₹0 / ₹10 / ₹20 cr in FY27-29E). Model EPS then equals profit attributable to owners ÷ 29.50 cr shares; model 'net profit' is that profit × 0.97.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹11 a share (interim ₹9 + final ₹2) = 17% of EPS; FY25 payout ~11-21%. We assume 18%.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash and essential, policy-supported demand, but earnings swing with subsidy rates, imported raw materials and the monsoon: slightly below market risk.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian fertiliser and crop-protection demand grows with farm output and prices; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Phosphatic demand grows ~3-4% in volume plus price; crop protection faster: 8% by year 12.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin was 10.3-11.3% in FY22-26 (14% in FY21): 11% long-run, as subsidy policy caps fertiliser returns.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 2.5% of revenue long-run (FY22-25 average ~2.6%), above depreciation at 2.0% to fund volume growth.
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period: the business is mature and net-cash, so no project J-curve to accommodate.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The government compensates the Middle East cost spike in the rabi NBS rates, raw-material prices normalise, own acid and Senegal rock lift fertiliser EBITDA towards ₹6,500/t, and crop protection compounds at 20%+.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Rabi subsidy rates stay inadequate while sulphur and ammonia stay high; a weak southern rabi after the 2026 monsoon cuts volumes; reasonable-margin guidelines cap fertiliser profits; NACL stalls.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Coromandel: Motilal Oswal 25x FY28E EPS (Jul-2026); earlier Sharekhan 26x FY28E and Nuvama 30x Q2FY28E (Dec-2025). 15x = the stock's 17.5x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 cut by the ~14% de-rating of Indian fertiliser and agrochemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026. Bull 19x (its five-year median trailing P/E: no de-rating, the market keeps paying for the agri-solutions story); bear 12x (the 2021 level, a plain fertiliser maker under subsidy stress).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the ~₹6,400 cr of Sep-28E net cash separately. 9x = the stock's 11.8x five-year median trailing EV/EBITDA less the ~22% EV/EBITDA de-rating of the same peers; it does not charge the step-up in depreciation (Senegal mine, NACL intangibles, acid plants).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: FCFF FY28-FY38E fading to an 11% EBITDA margin and capex at 2.5% of revenue, Ke 11.9% (beta 0.9), terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
